This is why the site earns the impression and never the citation on 3,896 US impressions a quarter.
recommendation: On the 67 decision-answer pages, set <title> to the question in its natural buyer phrasing ("Should we mandate API 510, 570 and 653 across a global portfolio?") and keep the declarative headline as the H2 immediately below the answer block. Do not restyle the 6,400 permutation pages — restrict this to the pages that already rank top-10 for a 12+ word query. Verify in dist/ after prerender, not the dev server: the React SEOHead layer is invisible to crawlers.

title: Answer blocks are definitional where the question is decisional — only 2% of conversational impressions reach a page that opens with a verdict
claim: The citation-spec answer block is well executed as a format but wrong in kind: 89% of conversational-query impressions land on a page with an answer block, yet only 2% land on one whose answer opens with a decision. The asker wants a recommendation; the page supplies a definition of the credential.
evidence: 88 landing pages carry the 132 long queries (3,383 impressions). 49 pages carry data-citation-block="answer" covering 3,020 impressions (89%), but only 5 pages — 52 impressions (2%) — open that block with a verdict (Yes/No/Mandate/Require/Choose/Use/Prioritise/Do not). Actual openers on the top landing pages: /api-510-certification (497 impr) "API ICP sets API 510 eligibility on a sliding scale..."; /api-inspector-guide (466 impr) "API 510 certifies in-service inspection of pressure vessels and heat exchangers..."; /api-570-certification (274 impr) "API 570 certifies the piping inspector: the person who...". The questions they were served for were "should we mandate", "do we accept... or do we hold the line", "is it still worth sponsoring at that cost". Site-wide there are only 269 unique decision-shaped headings across 7,155 pages, and 6 boilerplate strings account for 124 of the 396 occurrences (e.g. "Should I scan the whole site or start smaller?" repeated on 31 3d-scanning city pages). The format itself is sound — sampling 188 answer blocks gives a median of 57 words with 90% inside the spec's 40-70 band and 0% over 70 — so this is a rewrite of the first clause, not of the block.
businessImpact: An assistant composing an answer to "should we mandate API 510" needs a sentence it can quote as the recommendation. A definition of API 510 is available from API itself, ASME, and every training provider; it is not differentiating and gives the model no reason to name Atlantis. A defensible verdict written by an ASNT Level III is the only thing on this site an assistant cannot get elsewhere.
recommendation: Rewrite the opening clause of the answer block on the ~50 pages that serve 12+ word queries so it leads with the verdict and then the reasoning — the pattern /blog/should-we-mandate-api-510-570-653-portfolio-policy already uses ("Mandate API ICP by equipment class, not by headcount.") and /blog/asnt-level-iii-vs-api-qute-ultrasonic-scopes ("No. API consolidated QUTE, QUSE, QUPA and QUSE-PA into QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) in 2024..."). Keep the definitional sentence, move it to second position. Add a verdict-first check to scripts/lint-citation-spec.mjs so this cannot regress.

title: No page on the site emits max-snippet:-1 — the only robots directives present are 624 noindex tags
claim: Zero of 7,155 built pages carry max-snippet, max-image-preview or data-nosnippet. The 57-word answer blocks the site spent a programme building are subject to Google's default snippet cap, which is the same directive that governs how much of a page can be surfaced in AI Overviews and AI Mode.
evidence: dist/ scan: grep for 'max-snippet:-1' = 0 files; 'max-image-preview' = 0 files; 'data-nosnippet' = 0 files. The only <meta name="robots"> tags in the build are 623 instances of "noindex, follow" and 1 of "noindex, nofollow" — every one of the 6,531 indexable pages ships with no positive snippet directive at all. Sampled answer blocks run a median of 57 words (~380 characters), roughly 2.4x the default ~160-character snippet allowance. robots.txt is otherwise correctly configured and is not the blocker: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, DuckAssistBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Amazonbot and Applebot are all explicitly allowed.
businessImpact: This is the cheapest fix in the whole audit and it gates every other content investment. The answer block is the unit of text an assistant lifts; capping it at 160 characters truncates the verdict mid-sentence and removes the named authority reference that the citation spec was designed to place there. It applies uniformly across all 35,964 US impressions, not just the conversational subset.
recommendation: Add <meta name="robots" content="index, follow, max-snippet:-1, max-image-preview:large, max-video-preview:-1"> to the prerender head template in scripts/prerender.mjs, guarded so it never overwrites the 624 existing noindex tags. One edit, applies to 6,531 pages. Edit prerender.mjs with Edit/Write only — never a Python rewrite — and check the file size afterwards, since node --check reports SYNTAX OK on a truncated file.
